finding: حَتَّىٰ links the route begun in 18:85 to the arrival at مَغْرِبَ ٱلشَّمْسِ, making this a journey endpoint before the scene of finding and speech.
activation: The prior فَأَتْبَعَ سَبَبًا and the repeated arrival formula at the next two stations establish continuing movement.
limits: The particle marks an endpoint in the narrated journey; it does not by itself establish a symbolic boundary.

finding: إِذَا stages the arrival as the occasion for the subsequent findings: بَلَغَ is followed by وَجَدَهَا and وَوَجَدَ, rather than describing a habitual or merely hypothetical scene.

evidence.ar: إِذَا بَلَغَ مَغْرِبَ ٱلشَّمْسِ وَجَدَهَا تَغْرُبُ

activation: The perfect arrival verb and the sequential discovery clauses make the temporal scene concrete within the narrative.
limits: This describes the event as narrated; it does not independently establish a claim about the sun’s physical motion.

finding: بَلَغَ takes the named setting-place as its direct destination, and its repetition at the eastern and mountain-pass stations makes reaching a recurring structure for Dhū al-Qarnayn’s journey.
activation: The same arrival construction opens three successive stations in the surah.
limits: The physical reaching is active; broader senses such as maturity or attaining a degree do not have a clear local trigger, and responsibility is not encoded by the verb alone.

finding: مَغْرِبَ ٱلشَّمْسِ names the reached setting-place in a construct phrase; the following تَغْرُبُ repeats the root and joins destination to the sun’s setting there.
activation: The verb بَلَغَ governs the destination, then the setting verb echoes its root; the later sunrise station gives a paired horizon.
limits: Setting and disappearance are active in the wording; estrangement or unfamiliarity from other غ ر ب senses is not established here.

finding: ٱلشَّمْسِ completes the definite construct destination, and the feminine object suffix in وَجَدَهَا retrieves the sun as the object found setting.
activation: The construct phrase names the sun, and the next clause uses a feminine suffix before describing its setting.
limits: The sun is the direct narrative referent; the separate root sense of restiveness is not activated by this collocation.

finding: وَجَدَهَا makes the sun the object of finding, while تَغْرُبُ presents the state in which it is found: setting within Dhū al-Qarnayn’s narrated scene.
activation: The attached object suffix is followed immediately by the imperfect setting clause.
limits: The construction frames the report as an encounter; it does not say that Dhū al-Qarnayn caused the setting or settle its cosmological status.

finding: تَغْرُبُ portrays the sun’s setting as in progress within the وَجَدَهَا scene, echoing the root of مَغْرِبَ and connecting the reached place to the observed process.
activation: The imperfect verb follows the finding verb as its circumstantial state; the destination noun immediately precedes it.
limits: The setting and disappearance are clear; a further sense of social estrangement is not established by the root echo.

finding: فِى locates تَغْرُبُ in the spring-like locus, while عِندَهَا places the people near the scene; the two phrases distinguish containment from adjacency.

evidence.ar: تَغْرُبُ فِى عَيْنٍ حَمِئَةٍۢ وَوَجَدَ عِندَهَا قَوْمًا

activation: The setting verb takes فِى with the spring, and the second finding clause uses عِندَهَا for the people.
limits: فِى supports location within the spring image, but does not alone require a motion-into reading or assert that the sun physically enters water.

finding: عَيْنٍ names the locus as a spring in this phrase, while its eye sense remains a possible undertone in a scene organized around seeing and finding.
activation: The adjective حَمِئَةٍ identifies a physical quality of the locus; وَجَدَهَا and تَغْرُبُ keep perception salient.
limits: The spring sense is selected by the construction; the wording does not prove a deliberate eye or aperture metaphor.

finding: حَمِئَةٍ qualifies عَيْنٍ, attaching the muddy quality to the spring rather than to the sun. The supplied حَامِيَةٍ reading would instead describe a hot spring.
activation: The adjective agrees with the feminine genitive indefinite noun immediately before it, and the variant changes that description.
limits: The muddy and hot readings give different qualities of the locus; they should not be blended into one description.

finding: The coordinated وَوَجَدَ restarts the finding construction and moves the scene from the sun’s setting to the human encounter with قَوْمًا.

evidence.ar: وَجَدَهَا تَغْرُبُ فِى عَيْنٍ حَمِئَةٍۢ وَوَجَدَ عِندَهَا قَوْمًا

activation: The second وَجَدَ has a new overt object, قَوْمًا, after the first finding’s sun and setting clause.
limits: The coordination marks a shift in focus; it does not require a separate journey or a long interval between the two findings.
